statement: BTOS AI-use share in 2027Q4 is < 1.5x its 2025 average (Bloc A Census BTOS; 2027Q4)
status_at_phase_end: Shares the BTOS series (and its Nov-2025 wording break) with I-R2-02; same adoption family, count once. Outcome depends on the splice decision: (a) original-wording 2025 average ~8-9% -> 1.5x threshold ~13%; the new-wording series already reads 24.2% (Oct 19-Nov 1, 2026), so on a naive splice the indicator is far toward NO. (b) Re-baselined on new wording (2025 = Nov-Dec only, ~17.3-17.7%) -> threshold ~26%; latest 24.2% is +40% in ~11 months, and the 2026 trend (~+0.6 pt/month) would cross ~26% around early-mid 2027, also leaning NO but not decided. Method decision pending (see I-R2-02 notes).

items.summary: Statistics office changed the AI-use question from 'in producing goods or services' to 'in any business function' and started a new series from the 2025-11-17 collection; the 2025 baseline the indicator needs exists only on the old wording (plus two new-wording readings). Context item published before the phase.
items.detail: Bloc A Census Bureau 'BTOS AI Core Question Updates'. Same cluster as BF-2026-I-R2-02-001.

items.summary: Early 2026 new-wording reading ~17.7% (two weeks ending 2026-01-11), essentially flat vs the 17.3% Nov-2025 start - consistent with slow adoption at the start of the year.
items.detail: Bloc A Census BTOS biweekly; value via programs.com tracker. Release date approximate.

items.summary: Statistics office: AI use hovered at 17-20% from Dec 2025 to May 2026 (19.8% for period ending 2026-05-03); little change among firms with <20 employees. A plateau of this kind would favour YES on a re-baselined series.
items.detail: Bloc A Census Bureau story 'Large Firms With at Least 20 Employees Biggest AI Users' and BTOS data release 2026-05-07.

items.summary: Regional central-bank analysis: original-wording AI use in production ~10% in late 2025 (double mid-2024); broader wording ~20% in early 2026. Implies 2025 original-wording average ~8-9% and a 1.5x threshold of ~13%, already exceeded by any new-wording reading.
items.detail: Federal Reserve Bank of Minneapolis, 'AI adoption in business grows steadily but unevenly' (2026; day not verified). Same cluster as BF-2026-I-R2-02-005.

items.summary: Adoption re-accelerated in summer 2026: 21.5% (two weeks ending Jul 26), 21.8% (Aug 9), 22.4% (Aug 23).
items.detail: Bloc A Census BTOS biweekly via programs.com tracker table. Publication dates approximate (a few days after period end).

items.summary: Statistics office proposed moving generative-AI-use and AI-employment-impact questions into the core biweekly survey - a further possible wording change before 2027Q4 resolution.
items.detail: Federal Register 2026-18304, BTOS information-collection request (comments by 2026-10-09). Same cluster as BF-2026-I-R2-02-006.

items.summary: Latest reading before phase end: 24.2% of firms used AI (two weeks ending 2026-11-01; 24.6% two weeks earlier), 1.40x the Nov-2025 new-wording start (17.3%); expected use within six months 27.6%. Fastest gains among firms with 20-249 employees.
items.detail: Bloc A Census BTOS via programs.com tracker (updated 2026-11-06; verified). Sep 6 23.2%, Sep 20 23.8%, Oct 4 23.8%, Oct 18 24.6%, Nov 1 24.2%.

items.summary: No comparable high-frequency firm-AI-use series exists for Bloc B; indicator is single-jurisdiction.
items.detail: No NBS (Bloc B) biweekly/quarterly firm AI-adoption series found. Same cluster as BF-2026-I-R2-02-008.
